10.1002_adfm.78899: Prussian blue analogues (PBAs), especially low‐cost Mn‐doped Fe‐based PBAs, demonstrate significant potential for power‐type sodium‐ion batteries (SIBs), owing to their open framework and high theoretical capacity (∼170 mAh g −1 ). However, their capacity decay mechanisms, particularly under rapid charge/discharge conditions, remain insufficiently understood, hindering their practical implementation in high‐power energy storage systems. Here, we systematically investigate the failure mechanisms of Mn‐doped Fe‐based PBAs through multiple in/ex situ characterizations of Mn‐doped Fe‐PBA cathodes cycled under various current densities. Our analysis reveals that there are several pathways induce electrode degradation at high rate: (1) transition metal dissolution that disrupts redox‐active sites, (2) mechanical degradation that impairs electrode kinetics under high‐rate conditions, (3) severe and rapid Na dendrite growth, and (4) interfacial side reactions that generate a thick cathode‐electrolyte interphase layer. Rather than viewing transition metal dissolution and mechanical degradation as isolated degradation pathways, this study reveals that capacity collapse at 10 C is fundamentally driven by the intrinsic kinetic mismatch and mechanical failure, offering key insights for the design of durable, high‐power PBA‐based SIBs.
10.1002_smll.202507803: A sustainable strategy to mitigate nitrate (NO 3 − ) contamination in water involves its electrochemical reduction to ammonia (NH 3 ), a valuable green fuel. However, nitrate reduction reaction (NO 3 RR) is hindered by sluggish kinetics and poor selectivity due to the competing hydrogen evolution reaction (HER). Herein a strategic synthesis of a spinel high‐entropy oxide (HEAO) heterostructure is reported as an efficient electrocatalyst for NO 3 RR. The HEAO exhibits a Tafel slope of 275 mV dec −1 , a Faradaic efficiency of 84%, and an impressive NH 3 production rate of 314 µmol h −1 cm −2 at −0.6 V versus RHE. Mott–Schottky analysis reveals a high donor density and a low flat‐band potential, which contribute to the enhanced reaction kinetics. Hydrophobicity studies demonstrate that the water‐repellent nature of the HEAO suppresses the HER, favoring NO 3 RR selectivity. Finally, an energy conversion device based on this catalytic system is proposed, which delivers a promising open‐circuit potential of 0.61 V and a peak power density of 2.3 mW cm −2 at 27 mA cm −2 . A comprehensive density functional theory (DFT) analysis reveals that the Fe‐Mn bridge site in HEAO possesses optimal adsorption energy for NO 3 − ions and its capability to selectively reduce NO 3 − toward NH 3 .
10.1016_j.ecoenv.2026.120922: Polystyrene nanoplastics (PS-NPs), ubiquitous in natural environments, readily accumulate in organisms and pose emerging toxicological risks. This study pairs in vivo animal experiments assessing organ-specific oxidative stress responses induced by PS-NPs exposure with a descriptive random forest-based analysis of study-design variables reported in the published literature. Kunming mice were administered varying concentrations of PS-NPs with or without N-acetylcysteine (NAC) to assess oxidative stress across five organs (lung, liver, kidney, brain, and testicles). Dose-dependent increases in ROS and MDA, accompanied by GSH depletion, were observed in the lung, liver, kidney, and brain; testicles ROS and GSH followed similar trends, although MDA plateaued at the high dose without further significant increase. Additionally, pulmonary inflammatory cytokines (e.g., TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6) and histopathological examination revealed dose-dependent lung injury, which was also significantly alleviated by NAC co-administration. A descriptive literature mining further illustrated the current distribution of study design variables across organ-specific investigations, highlighting the existing research focus and knowledge gaps in PS-NPs toxicology. Collectively, this work demonstrates the complementary value of pairing toxicological experimentation with descriptive literature analysis to decipher nanoplastic health risks and highlights the promise of data-driven analysis for toxicology and environmental health assessment.
10.1039_d6cc04089f: The loading of peroxyoxalate into a molecularly imprinted gel greatly improved its hydrophilicity, achieving intense (70-fold enhancement) and persistent (> 1 h) chemiexcitation of carbon dots under physiological conditions. Additionally, the gel could be readily refueled by reloading peroxyoxalate into the imprinted cavities. The system was quite suitable for chemiluminescent sensing.
10.1039_d6ta03417a: A novel 1D/2D α-FeOOH/PSCN S-scheme heterojunction was constructed, where a robust internal electric field drives efficient photo-Fenton degradation of antibiotic pollutants.
10.5194_hess-29-6069-2025: Research into rapid transitions between hydrological drought and flood is growing in popularity, in part due to media-reported catastrophic impacts from recent events. Droughts and floods are typically studied as events that are independent from one another, and thus, a clear definition and assessment of the methods used to define consecutive drought-to-flood transition events does not yet exist. In this paper, we use a series of eight catchments that have experienced real-world impacts from drought-to-flood transitions as case studies to assess the suitability of, and differences between, different event selection methods applied to observational data. We demonstrate that different threshold level methods can result in the selection of different drought and flood events. When combined this can influence the number, seasonality and characteristics of detected drought-to-flood transitions. The time period used to define the maximum interval between drought and flood also influences whether transitions are detected. We show that the probability of a transition occurring within a set time window could vary substantially between different methodologies. The differences in detected events are especially apparent in highly seasonal flow regimes. We also show that previously applied methodologies likely fail to detect transition events that have been broadly impactful in the historical record. Further, we qualitatively assess the streamflow time series of the case study catchments, and outline a number of potential pitfalls in the event detection process. Finally, we make recommendations regarding methodological choices in the context of potential impacts of interest, and outline some priorities for future methodological development and research into transitions.
